Solution 2 has the correct answer, 171.

**Reduction.** Ana fails on a pair of primes $\{p,q\}$ exactly when some nonconstant $p$-periodic $f$ and nonconstant $q$-periodic $g$ agree on the queried points. Build the bipartite graph between residues mod $p$ and residues mod $q$, with one edge per queried point. Agreement means $f$ and $g$ take constant values on each connected component. Such a pair exists iff both primes have at least two components containing their residues. So Ana wins on $\{p,q\}$ iff, for one of the two primes, every residue is queried and all of them lie in a single component.

**Lower bound.** At most one prime can be "not fully covered," since two such primes always leave a bad pair. The two largest fully covered primes need a connected bipartite graph, which requires at least $p+q-1$ distinct edges. Excluding 97 gives the smallest requirement, $83+89-1=171$. Every other choice of excluded prime gives at least 179, so $n\ge 171$.

**Upper bound.** Take the 171 integers $0,1,\dots,170$ with their residues mod 97 all set to 0 (via CRT, residues mod different primes can be chosen independently). For primes $p,q\le 89$, connectivity of the graph on $\{0,\dots,170\}$ with edges of difference $p$ or $q$ follows from Fine–Wilf, since $170\ge p+q-2$ holds for all such pairs. Each $p\le 89$ is fully covered because $171\ge p$. For pairs involving 97, the graph is a star centred on the single residue 0 mod 97, so it is connected and $p$ is fully covered. Hence $n=171$ works.

Solutions 1 and 3 give 186 and 185, which are too large. Solution 2's reasoning is sketchy in places (the simultaneous construction is argued loosely), but its final answer is right.

CHOICE: 2
